notes: AN ADVANCE WHOSE CHEQUE NEVER REACHED THE REGISTER IS NOW NAMED. Issuing an advance does two things: it posts the entry to your books, and it puts the cheque on the register. If the second one did not finish — the app was closed, the machine slept, something interrupted it — you were left with a state nothing could see. The receivable and the general ledger agree with each other, so every balance check stayed quiet, and the only sign was a bank reconciliation that would not come out with nothing saying why. The health check now reads staff advances the way it has read payments since August: an advance whose own record NAMES a cheque, on a posted entry, with no row on the register, is reported by name and amount with what to do about it. It stays quiet where nothing is wrong — an advance recorded without a cheque number, a draft that has not paid anyone, and an advance that has been reversed are all left alone. A warning that goes off when nothing is wrong is worse than no warning at all. ALSO IN THIS BUILD, FROM 0.8.94: VAT — YOU RECLAIM THE WHOLE CHARGE FROM 2026. The Value Added Tax Act, 2025 (Act 1151) took effect on 1 January 2026. It abolished the COVID-19 levy, recoupled the NHIL and the GETFund levy to the VAT base, and made both deductible as input tax — they were not before. If you are VAT-registered you now reclaim the whole charge on a purchase rather than fifteen points of it, so your costs and your VAT position are both stated correctly. NOTHING ALREADY IN YOUR BOOKS IS RESTATED: which treatment applies is decided by the date on the document, so a bill dated before 2026 keeps the treatment it was entered under and no figure you have already recorded moves. NO DATA CHANGE — this installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
